title: Session Zero - Prologue
summary:
It is the sixty-third year of the Fourth Age.
Middle-earth is at peace.
The kingdoms of Men are well-established, the great wars lie a lifetime behind most folk, and the roads between friendly lands are once again kept and patrolled. Travelers move freely, inns are open, and the world has settled into a long season of rebuilding and remembrance.
Yet peace does not mean perfection.
The Shadow is gone, but the world is still wide. There are empty places where watch is thin, old roads that see little traffic, and the occasional trouble that comes not from evil design, but from neglect, greed, or what the wild has yet to fully forget. Important journeys are still made with care — not out of fear, but good sense.
It is for this reason that you have been asked to travel to the Shire.
Among the Hobbits, a careful copy of the Red Book of Westmarch has long been kept — a faithful record of the great deeds and small hands that helped bring an age to its close. This copy, prepared in the Shire and later annotated in Gondor, is known as the Thain’s Book: a work of history, memory, and quiet pride.
At the request of Aragorn Elessar, the Thain’s Book is now to be brought south, to be preserved in the archives of Minas Tirith, alongside the great histories of Elves, Dwarves, and Men.
The Shire agreed readily — but chose its manner carefully.
Rather than send the book with a caravan or under formal guard, it was decided it should travel as Hobbits prefer all meaningful things to travel: quietly, respectfully, and in good company.
That is where you come in.
You have been chosen not because the road is dangerous, but because the task matters. You are trusted travelers — steady folk, accustomed to the road, able to offer protection if needed and discretion always. You are as much there for the people as for the book itself.
For Meriadoc Brandybuck and Peregrin Took, now well into their later years, will accompany the Book on its journey. Once they crossed Middle-earth in days of war; now they travel at an easier pace, content with conversation, good meals, and the company of those they trust.
Your charge is clear.
Travel with Merry and Pippin from the Shire.
 See the Thain’s Book safely through Rohan.
 And deliver it, intact and untroubled, to Minas Tirith.
This is not a mission born of fear.
 It is a duty born of respect — for history, for friendship, and for the understanding that even in peace, some things deserve careful hands.
And so you leave your homes behind—not as heroes riding to war, but as companions who have said their farewells. Each of you leaves something precious in your care: a loved one, a quiet life, an unfinished hope, or a promise to return. The road ahead is gentle, but the parting is real—and it is that choice which gives the journey its weight.
The journey begins in green hills, under open skies,
 with good company…
 and a story worth carrying forward.
